3.8 FLOWCHART
The diagrams separate access and registration, role navigation, and course enrollment details.
Oval terminators identify the start or end; rectangles identify processes; parallelograms identify
input/output; diamonds identify decisions; and rectangles with double side lines identify detailed
subprocesses. Circles continue a flow on the same page, while pentagonal connectors continue it on
another diagram. Matching letters identify the destination. Each protected operation remains subject
to backend authorization.
Figure 3
Symbols used in the system flowcharts
Off-page connectors R and L link registration with the access chart; S, I, A and U link to
Student, Instructor, Administrator and Super User overviews. E and E2 lead to the enrollment request
and Instructor review details. Same-page pairs L1, R1 and E1 allow correction and retry; S1, I1, A1
and U1 return to the corresponding dashboard. A dashed line marks the later review of a recorded
pending request, which does not block the Student from using other modules.

3.8.1 Account Access and Registration
Figure 4
Account access and role routing
Users open the appropriate client and authenticate using email, password and institute
selection. The backend validates credentials, account status, role and permitted institute before
establishing a session. Invalid access produces feedback and a retry through L1. The target release
routes successful access to the appropriate role overview. New public Student or Instructor accounts

use R; privileged accounts are created through authorized administrative operations. The Super User
routing branch represents the agreed expansion and must be verified in the evaluation release.

Figure 5
Public Student and Instructor registration detail
The registration process validates required fields, institute, permitted public role and duplicate
email. Invalid input returns through R1 for correction. Valid registration hashes the password, creates
the account, and displays confirmation. L returns to the access chart. Email verification or approval
steps may be documented only when they exist in the evaluated registration workflow; no user-
entered security pass-token is assumed.

3.8.2 Student View
Figure 6
Student overview with links to detailed enrollment
S opens the Student Dashboard after successful access or a completed enrollment action.
Students select approved coursework and assigned deadlines, request enrollment, view their own
grades, and use permitted study, calendar, coding and collaboration tools. Personal Tasks remain
separate from the academic To-Do list. Each ordinary module returns through S1; Join Courses
continues through E. Students do not gain faculty-directory or supervisory privileges. Log out ends
the session.

Figure 7
Student course enrollment request detail
E receives the Join Courses action. The backend checks the code, institute and existing
enrollment status. Invalid or duplicate requests produce feedback and retry through E1. An eligible
request is saved as PENDING, then shown to the Student. S returns to the Student overview without
granting course access. E2 identifies the Instructor’s later review of the saved request.

Figure 8
Instructor enrollment decision detail
The assigned Instructor opens the request queue and the backend checks authority and the
current request state. Approval saves APPROVED and grants enrolled-course access; rejection saves
REJECTED and does not grant access. Updated status becomes available through the Student’s
permitted course view. I returns to the Instructor overview. A valid course code alone does not enroll
the Student immediately.

3.8.3 Instructor View
Figure 9
Instructor overview with enrollment review continuation
I opens the Instructor Dashboard. Instructors manage assigned courses and resources,
configure grades, inspect descriptive analytics, review enrollment requests through E2, and assess
CodeLab results or Git-linked work through their separate workflows. Calendar and faculty-directory
actions follow their permissions; Program Head publishing requires that designation. Moderation,
verification and owned study functions remain bounded by their rules. I1 returns to the dashboard,
while Log out ends the session.

3.8.4 Administrator View
Figure 10
Native Administrator Console overview
A opens the native Administrator Console after validated Administrator access. Supported
actions include accounts and roles, academic configuration, schedule/event administration, audit
review, reports and continuity functions. Only authorized Administrators provision or revoke Super
User accounts. Historical audit records are reviewed rather than freely rewritten. A1 returns to the
dashboard. The researchers will verify these restricted functions with controlled accounts; no separate
Administrator respondent group is introduced.

3.8.5 Super User View
Figure 11
Restricted Super User academic operations overview
U opens the web-based academic operations hub for an authorized institute. The Super User
uses permitted faculty and leadership information, reads timetables, publishes permitted shared
events, inspects safe course summaries, and manages owned private records. Supervision excludes
student identities, individual grades, submissions, attempts and answers. The role does not permit
grading, assessment participation, schedule editing or generic administration. U1 returns to the hub;
Log out ends the session. This expansion will undergo researcher-conducted technical checks.

3.9 ENTITY RELATIONSHIP DIAGRAM
The ERDs present selected relationships from the current Prisma schema and a separate target
diagram for the coordination expansion. User stores account roles; Student, Instructor and
Administrator are not independent account tables. Repeated entities across figures refer to the same
logical table. PK denotes a primary key, FK a foreign key and UK a unique key or combination.
Crow’s-foot notation shows multiplicity: a circle indicates zero, a bar indicates one, and a fork
indicates many. Optional child collections may contain zero records.

Figure 12
Account, institute and course enrollment relationships
Institute links User and Course records. Course.instructorId is optional and references a User
acting as Instructor. Enrollment links a Student User to a Course and stores pending, approved or
rejected status under a unique course/student pair. Session records belong to User. Role and resource
authorization are enforced separately from these foreign-key links.

Figure 13
Coursework, submission and grading relationships
Course links SyllabusItem records and an optional GradingPolicy. CategoryWeight records
define the policy’s component weights. StudentSubmission connects an item to a Student User, with
a unique item/student pair and recorded grade or status. Computed grade summaries use the
applicable grading rules; they are not modelled as a single undifferentiated Grade table.

Figure 14
Selected personal ownership and learning activity relationships
User owns Note and CalendarEvent records, creates FlashcardDeck records, and creates
ActivityTemplate records through createdBy. CalendarEvent may optionally reference Course, while
ActivityTemplate requires a courseId. These selected relationships omit supporting task, card,
progress, study-session and gamification tables for readability; their fields and constraints remain part
of the release schema.

Figure 15
Separate programming, repository and forum record relationships
ActivityTemplate links ActivitySubmission records containing scores and execution-related
outcomes. GithubRepoLink links GithubSubmission records, which also reference the submitting
User and SyllabusItem. KxPost links KxAnswer records with an author and optional verifying faculty
User. These groups preserve the distinction between code execution, Git coursework and moderated
discussion.

Figure 16
Proposed coordination schema and private snapshot relationships
Dashed outlines distinguish the target additions from current schema records. CourseSchedule
and CourseScheduleException will preserve effective-dated revisions and occurrence exceptions.
Course and User will receive program and coordination fields. CalendarEvent will receive time,
audience, source-note and version fields; Note will receive an event-source link with a unique
creator/event combination. Institute.deanId and other membership/attribution links will be checked
against the final migration. Snapshot conversions are one-time copies, not ongoing synchronization.
